themes_detail.label: Park Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints spiked to 3 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2,300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting a new disturbance pattern or event in Fort Greene or Brooklyn Heights parks that warrants immediate investigation into what's changed.
evidence: 3 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% spike)
z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically significant anomaly
No prior pattern suggests sudden behavioral or operational change in district parks
reporting_angles: Visit Fort Greene Park and Brooklyn Heights Promenade this week to observe current noise sources (construction, events, vendor activity, music)
Interview Parks Department about any permitted events, maintenance schedules, or vendor licensing changes in the past 7 days

themes_detail.label: Dead Trees Surge
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints jumped to 8 last week versus a baseline of 1.4 per week—a 482% increase (z-score: 5.96)—potentially signaling environmental stress, pest infestation, or deferred maintenance in the district's street tree inventory.
evidence: 8 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (482% spike)
z-score of 5.96 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Community board has repeatedly requested 'new equipment for maintenance' from Parks Department, suggesting chronic underfunding
reporting_angles: Obtain GPS locations of 8 reported trees and photograph conditions; cross-reference with Parks Department tree maintenance records
Contact Parks Department arborist to determine if this reflects a specific pest outbreak (Asian longhorned beetle, etc.) or systemic maintenance backlog

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Rising
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints spiked to 4 last week versus 0.5 weekly average—a 700% increase (z-score: 7.0)—suggesting renewed tensions over restaurant sheds, seating, or vendor management in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights as warmer weather returns.
evidence: 4 outdoor dining complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike)
z-score of 7.0 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Spike coincides with seasonal warming and likely reopening/expansion of outdoor seating
reporting_angles: Map the 4 complaints by location; identify specific restaurants and their current outdoor dining footprints
Interview affected residents on sidewalk obstruction, noise, or sanitation issues; contact SLA about any licensing changes or enforcement actions

themes_detail.label: Homelessness Assistance Spike
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints jumped to 35 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 11.6 per week—a 201% increase (z-score: 6.25)—indicating a possible encampment growth, behavioral crisis, or service gap in the district.
evidence: 35 homeless person assistance complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 11.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (201% spike)
z-score of 6.25 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Community board has ongoing requests for senior center and social services funding
reporting_angles: Conduct street-level reporting on Fort Greene Park, Brooklyn Heights Promenade, and transit hubs to observe encampment density and conditions
Interview NYPD, DHS, and local shelter operators on whether a specific incident, service closure, or seasonal pattern triggered the spike

themes_detail.label: Door/Window Damage Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Door and window complaints surged to 18 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 6.2 per week—a 188% increase (z-score: 5.16)—potentially reflecting a targeted break-in pattern, weather event, or vandalism wave requiring public safety review.
evidence: 18 door/window complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 6.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (188% spike)
z-score of 5.16 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Suggests either crime pattern, weather damage, or construction-related incidents
reporting_angles: Map the 18 complaints by address and determine if they cluster geographically (suggesting targeted burglary) or are dispersed (suggesting weather or construction)
Cross-reference with NYPD crime data and 311 street/sidewalk noise spikes to determine if construction debris is causing impact damage
